hints: Differentiate $V = \frac{4}{3}(25+h)^3 - \frac{62500}{3}$ with respect to $h$ using the chain rule.
Relate the rates of change using the chain rule: $\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{dV}{dh} \times \frac{dh}{dt}$, given $\frac{dV}{dt} = 500\text{ cm}^3\text{s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
Differentiate the volume formula $V(h)$ with respect to $h$:
$$\frac{dV}{dh} = \frac{4}{3} \cdot 3(25 + h)^2 = 4(25 + h)^2$$

Evaluate $\frac{dV}{dh}$ at the instant when $h = 10\text{ cm}$:
$$\left.\frac{dV}{dh}\right|_{h=10} = 4(25 + 10)^2 = 4(35^2) = 4(1225) = 4900\text{ cm}^2$$

Apply the chain rule to relate the time derivatives:
$$\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{dV}{dh} \cdot \frac{dh}{dt} \implies 500 = 4900 \cdot \frac{dh}{dt}$$

Solve for the rate of increase of depth $\frac{dh}{dt}$:
$$\frac{dh}{dt} = \frac{500}{4900} = \frac{5}{49} \approx 0.102\text{ cm s}^{-1}$$

hints: Use the chain rule $\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{dV}{dh} \times \frac{dh}{dt}$ with $\frac{dV}{dt} = 500$ and $\frac{dh}{dt} = 0.075$ to find $(25+h)^2$.
Substitute $(25+h)$ into the volume formula $V = \frac{4}{3}(25+h)^3 - \frac{62500}{3}$ and compute the value.
walkthrough:
Set up the rate equation using the chain rule with $\frac{dh}{dt} = 0.075\text{ cm s}^{-1}$:
$$\frac{dV}{dt} = 4(25 + h)^2 \cdot \frac{dh}{dt} \implies 500 = 4(25 + h)^2 (0.075) = 0.3(25 + h)^2$$
